trashwheelexplorer

Overview

trashwheelexplorer is an R package for exploring rubbish collection patterns in Baltimore’s waterways.

This package includes a prepared data set, a summary function, and an interactive Shiny app that allows users to compare estimated rubbish counts across Trash Wheels and across time.

The package documentation, function reference pages, and vignette are available on the pkgdown website.

Intended user & research question

Intended user: environmental officers working with Baltimore’s Healthy Harbour initiative.

Research question: how have the types and estimated quantities of rubbish collected by Baltimore’s Trash Wheels varied across locations and over time?

The Shiny app helps users delve into these patterns through visualisations, interactive filters, and a summary table.

Data

This package contains trash_collections which is a data set sourced from TidyTuesday on the 5th March of 2024. The original data came from Baltimore’s Healthy Harbour initiative, which operates four Trash Wheels to collect rubbish from waterways.

The prepared data set contains 6,951 rows and 11 variables. Each row represents one rubbish category for one dumpster collection. The data includes collection dates, Trash Wheel names, weight, volume, and estimated amount of seven rubbish categories.

Data preparation

The data are prepared reproducibly using: data-raw/trash_collections.R. The script imports the source CSV, standardises column names, parses collection dates, and reshapes rubbish categories into long format using pivot_longer().

The prepared data are stored in data/trash_collections.rda.

Limitations

Rubbish item counts are estimates, not exact counts. Missing counts do not necessarily indicate zero rubbish.

The number of collections differs across Trash Whels and years, so raw totals are not always directly comparable.

In the long-format data set, collection-level weight and volume are repeated across rubbish categories and should not be summed across these repeated rows.

Installation

Install the development package from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-ca-ryn")

Usage

Load the package:

library(trashwheelexplorer)

Access the data set 

head(trash_collections)

Summarise rubbish collections 

summarise_trash(trash_collections)

Identify the three Trash Wheel-year groups with the highest estimated plastic bottle counts:

summarise_trash(trash_collections) |>
  dplyr::filter(trash_type == "plastic_bottles") |>
  dplyr::slice_max(total_estimated, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE)

Launch the Shiny app 

run_app()

The app allows users to:

  • Select one or more Trash Wheels.
  • Filter collections by year(s).
  • Choose a rubbish category.
  • Compare average estimated item counts using charts.
  • Examine detailed collection summaries and missing counts.

Data sources

  • TidyTuesday (2024): Trash Wheel Collection Data
  • Original source: Baltimore Healthy Harbour
